profile.reading:
Csquare IAD1-C sits at 21110 Ridgetop Circle, Sterling, Virginia 20166, one of three buildings (IAD1-A, IAD1-B, IAD1-C) on Csquare's IAD1 campus in Loudoun County's Northern Virginia data center corridor. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists IAD1-C individually at 57,444 square feet sellable, 60.4 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, the largest of the three IAD1 buildings by that measure; Csquare's public spec sheet gives only a combined campus total across all three IAD1 buildings, 141,621 square feet of raised floor, 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity, with chilled-water cooling and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, and ENERGY STAR certifications applicable campus-wide rather than broken out per building. All three IAD1 buildings are leased rather than Csquare-owned, per the SEC filing. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for IAD1-C; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD1 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, alongside dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing notes the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked in this dataset.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 95 (Centersquare): operator market page gives one combined Sterling IAD1 figure for what this registry splits into three clustered rows, combined figure recorded as context only and not applied per row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete, no address applied.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Centersquare. This session found that centersquaredc.com, the legacy domain matching this registry entire Centersquare operator bucket naming, now issues a live redirect to www.csquare.com, the operator current domain, confirmed directly this session. Csquare own site states it owns and operates data centers built over decades by developing, acquiring, integrating, and operating advanced data centers, without giving a specific founding or rebrand date on the pages fetched this session. Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. This row is one of three registry rows under this operator in Sterling, VA carrying an IAD1 prefixed code, IAD1-A, IAD1-B, and IAD1-C, whose coordinates in this registry all fall within roughly 250 meters of each other. The operator own current market page for Northern Virginia, fetched this session, describes only a single combined Sterling IAD1 facility figure, 143.2 MW of utility power and 141,621 square feet of raised floor, with no A, B, or C subdivision mentioned and no street address published. This session could not determine whether the three clustered registry rows represent three distinct buildings on one campus sharing that single published figure, or an over fragmented recording of what is now marketed as one consolidated facility, so the combined figure is recorded here as market level context only and is not applied as this specific row own individual capacity or square footage, flagged for a future researcher to disaggregate or consolidate as appropriate.

reading.body:
Centersquare IAD1-C in Sterling, Virginia is one of three clustered facilities under the same operator in this location, but published specifications do not include individual capacity figures for this building. The operator's market page lists a combined 143.2 MW of utility power and 141,621 square feet of raised floor across all three Sterling IAD1 facilities without subdivision, making it impossible from published data to determine what fraction belongs to this specific campus.

At common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the combined 143.2 MW Sterling IAD1 figure would support roughly 3,600 racks, but this reading cannot be assigned to IAD1-C alone. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities and 1,375 MW of published utility capacity across 23 that disclose figures. This campus ranks 24th among Virginia's published capacity, below the state's disclosed supply, suggesting the combined Sterling figure either remains undisclosed in finer detail or has not been counted in state totals.

The facility itself is verified through OpenStreetMap and carries an address in Sterling's technology corridor. No certifications, power quality specifications, cooling design, or grid connection details are published. Whether this campus qualifies for any particular AI workload cannot be read from the available data.
